_comment: The template languages this extension contributes. This table is the source of truth: `node scripts/languages/generate.mjs` expands it into package.json (contributes.languages, grammars, snippets), one syntaxes/askama-<name>.tmLanguage.json per language, the injection grammar's selector and src/languages.ts. Adding a language means adding one entry here and re-running that. `id` is the VS Code language id and `name` its display name after `Askama `. `scope` is the scope the language's grammar registers. `host` is the TextMate scope of the format being templated; its grammar colours everything outside the Askama tags. `bundled` marks a language whose grammar file is written by hand because no host grammar exists to include — the generator leaves that file alone. A language with neither is plain text: its grammar is `source.askama` alone and nothing is injected into it. `provider: extension` marks a host grammar VS Code does not ship, so the host part stays uncoloured until the user installs an extension for it; src/contributions.test.ts checks every other host against the VS Code on the machine running the tests. `extensions`, `filenames` and `filenamePatterns` list base names; each is expanded with every entry of `suffixes`, so `.html` claims `.html.askama`, `.html.j2`, `.html.jinja` and `.html.jinja2`.
